title_en: Chinese Science Fiction (15/20): The Delivery Robots' Strike
note_en: Look at 才 in 机器人们才重新开始工作 "only then did the robots go back to work." Placed before the verb, 才 means the action happened later than expected, only after a condition was met (here, the company giving in). English needs a phrase like "only then" or "not until," often with inverted word order, while Chinese just slips 才 in front of the verb; compare 就, which signals that something happened early or easily.
